This document is the synthesis of a three-model review of
**renting~thefloorwip~.org**. It is deliberately separate from the
essay: the essay carries 194 inline reviewer comments; this is the
editorial verdict and the prioritized fix list. Read it as the review,
not as the essay.

# 1. The Verdict

## 1.1 The idea versus the execution

The idea and the execution are at two different levels, and they must
not be conflated.

**The idea is a 9.** \"India rents the floor\" is a genuinely original,
memorable thesis. The layered metaphor (Raw Material -\> Plumbing -\>
Floor -\> Building -\> Interior) is the cleanest analytical frame for
the India-vs-China software question I have seen. And the reframed
version --- *India did not avoid the wall; it answered it by assembly
instead of greenfield sovereignty* --- is both more honest and more
interesting than the \"India never hit a wall\" line it replaced. That
reframe is the single best sentence in the essay.

**The execution is a 5.** The argument is carried almost entirely on
numbers, and too many of those numbers are wrong, stale, mislabeled, or
unsourced. The essay levels the accusation of \"assertion without
verification\" at Indian software policy; as it currently stands, a
hostile reader can level the same accusation back at the essay, with
receipts. That is the one thing standing between this and publication.

## 1.2 The uncomfortable truth

If a serious editor received this today, their first three questions
would all be the same kind: \"Where did 26.7 million developers come
from?\" \"Why does your GitHub topics table not match the raw CSV?\"
\"Why is a US-founded database listed as an Indian re-domiciliation?\"
The thesis would survive those questions. The credibility of the
evidence base, as written, would not.

The essay was drafted before the data was verified. This is the root
cause of nearly every problem below, and it is why the fix list is long:
not because the thinking is weak, but because the facts were treated as
decoration rather than as the load-bearing structure they actually are.

# 2. Areas of Improvement --- prioritized

## 2.1 P0 --- factual errors (fix before anything else)

1.  \"The largest open-source contributor base by headcount\" (Sec 3.8)
    and \"#1 OSS Contributors\" (Paradox figure). **Wrong.** GitHub
    Innovation Graph Q1 2026: US 32.4M \> India 26.7M. India is #2 by
    headcount; its defensible #1 claims are growth and annual additions.
    Reword to \"one of the largest\" or \"fastest growing.\"

2.  The GitHub topics table (Sec 5.1.004) is presented as \"not
    hand-picked --- raw Innovation Graph output.\" **It is not.** The
    raw CSV shows \"rust\" never in China\'s top-12, \"golang\" only in
    Q1; India\'s actual top topics are python and javascript, both
    omitted. Worse, China\'s raw top topics are also mostly web
    languages --- so the table, even corrected, does not prove the
    \"China=systems-languages\" story it is built to support. Rewrite
    from the raw CSV or relabel as illustrative. This is the single most
    damaging item: a knowledgeable reader will check it and stop
    trusting the rest.

3.  \"MapMyIndia (now KOO)\" (Sec 5.4.2.2, three places). **Wrong.**
    MapMyIndia = CE Info Systems (founded 1995, consumer brand Mappls);
    Koo = a microblogging app (launched 2020, dead July 2024).
    Unrelated. Remove \"(now KOO)\".

4.  \"AdventNet founded in Chennai\" (Sec 5.2.2, body, timeline figure,
    and DESCRIPTION). **Wrong.** Founded/incorporated in New Jersey,
    USA, 1996; Chennai is the later R&D hub. Fix all three occurrences.

5.  \"OceanBase ... now governed by Apache\" (Sec 6.4.4.2) and \"donated
    to Apache or CNCF\" (Sec 6.5). **Wrong.** OceanBase is Mulan PSL /
    OpenAtom Foundation; only RocketMQ is an Apache TLP. The error
    recurs in two sections --- fix both.

6.  \"Baidu (Hadoop)\" in the pattern-mapping table (Sec 6.3).
    **Wrong.** Hadoop was Doug Cutting at Yahoo!, not Baidu; the
    essay\'s own canonical table (Sec 6.2.1) says so. Replace with a
    real Chinese scale-problem build (e.g. Alibaba MaxCompute) or drop
    the cell.

7.  The \"\~34 million TPM / \~150×\" UPI gap (Sec 3.7.001 Q1). **Units
    error.** 2,055M tpmC is \~2,055 million per **minute** (\~34M per
    **second**). The gap vs UPI\'s \~224K TPM is \~9,000×, not 150×. The
    essay understates its own point by \~60×.

8.  The wall thesis contradicts itself. Executive Summary (i) now
    correctly says \"India did hit walls (PhonePe/Mesos, Zerodha) but
    answered by assembly,\" yet Sec 6.1 still says \"India faced none\"
    and \"India never hit a wall,\" and Sec 6.8 repeats \"we have not
    hit a wall.\" Reconcile all three to the reframed thesis.

9.  \"YugabyteDB ... re-domiciled to the US\" (Sec 6.4.4.1 and the Exec
    Summary\'s implied \"India did produce builders\"). **Wrong.**
    YugabyteDB and MinIO were US-founded; Hasura is the one genuine
    re-domiciliation. Fix the list, and either label YugabyteDB \"a US
    software company used as a foil\" or remove it from the
    Indian-builders list.

10. Drove described two ways: Sec 6.7 calls it a manager \"of Kubernetes
    clusters\"; Sec 6.4.4.2 (correctly) calls it a
    Kubernetes/Mesos-class orchestrator built to **replace** Mesos. Fix
    Sec 6.7 --- Drove does not sit on top of Kubernetes.

11. OceanBase attribution is inconsistent: \"Ant Group\" (Sec 6.2.1
    table, 6.2.4) versus \"Alibaba\" (Sec 3.5). OceanBase began inside
    Alibaba in 2010; Ant adopted it later. Pick one and make every
    occurrence consistent.

12. TPC-C dates. **Do not change them.** Two of the three prior
    reviewers \"corrected\" the Bull Escala / OceanBase / TDSQL dates;
    those corrections are wrong --- they confused TPC.org\'s \"System
    Availability\" column with \"Date Submitted.\" The essay\'s dates
    (Jun 2008, May 2020, Mar 2023) are correct as submitted. If
    anything, add a note that dates are \"Date Submitted.\"

## 2.2 P1 --- wrong, stale, or mislabeled data

1.  \"26.7 million developers\" is undefined. It sits across three
    incompatible metrics: GitHub Innovation Graph 26.7M (Q1 2026),
    GitHub Octoverse \~21.9M \"builders,\" NASSCOM 5.8M employed. State
    the metric and cite the source.

2.  \"5.2 million new developers a year\" is metric-mixing. That is
    GitHub new-account growth (Octoverse), not net employment ---
    NASSCOM\'s entire workforce is 5.8M. Label it or drop it.

3.  Export share \"\~86%\" is wrong. NASSCOM FY25: \~\$224bn exports of
    \$282.6bn = \~79%. Fix the body, the chart literal (value:86), and
    footnote 2.

4.  Revenue segment breakdown is mislabeled. \"\$55bn Software
    Products\" is actually \~BPM; \"Engineering/R&D \$15bn\" is far too
    low (\~\$50bn); \"IT Services \$210bn\" inflated. Correct to
    NASSCOM\'s real breakouts or mark the whole chart \[Author
    judgement\], not just the foundational slice.

5.  R&D/GDP figures are stale. Current (World Bank): China 2.58%, India
    0.65%, US 3.45%, Korea 4.94%. The table\'s US 2.8 and Korea 4.2 are
    \~5-7 years old.

6.  Zoho timeline dates: ManageEngine launched 2002 (not 2005); \"Zoho
    brand\" launched 2005 (2009 was the rename to Zoho Corporation).
    Relabel both.

7.  UPI \"\~500 million transactions/day\" is stale --- UPI crossed 20
    billion/month (\~645M/day) in Aug 2025. The \"₹314 lakh crore/year\"
    figure is correct for the latest full year (FY26) but needs the
    period label and an NPCI citation.

8.  OceanBase license: the repo is now Apache-2.0 (GitHub API), not
    Mulan PL. Say \"initially MulanPubL-2.0, since re-licensed to
    Apache-2.0.\"

9.  Drove has no license file (GitHub API license = null). \"Apache
    2.0\" and \"permissive license\" are both unsupported. Either add
    the LICENSE file or correct the text.

10. Aadhaar \"\~1.3bn\" understates --- UIDAI reports \~1.39bn. Minor,
    but fix while you are in there.

## 2.3 P2 --- claims that need sources or qualification

1.  ShaktiDB has no public repository or official page. A named,
    checkable project (MeitY-funded, June 2025) with no URL is a
    liability. Mark \"as announced to the author\" or remove from
    tables.

2.  The Zepto upstream-PR story is unverifiable --- no Zepto engineering
    post or PostgreSQL commit exists. Tag \[Author judgement\] as an
    illustrative fable, or replace with a verified upstream-contribution
    example.

3.  The \"unicorn that rented the floor\" names no company. A story with
    \"\$500M raised, 10M users, acquired 2019 at 10%\" and no name reads
    as fabricated. Label it \"Illustrative / Composite\" explicitly.

4.  \"Zoho built its own OS\" overstates. Sourced (ToI 21 Jul 2023; ET
    CIO), but it is \"building/announced,\" not \"built,\" and it is a
    laptop OS, not a server or kernel OS.

5.  \"Zoho has 50 million users\" is stale --- Zoho claims 100M+ since
    \~2023.

6.  The 55% delivery / 5.5% value / 10.5% exports / 0.3% royalties
    figures are load-bearing but mostly uncited. Cite each (NASSCOM,
    Everest, IMF BOP) or tag \[Author judgement\].

7.  \"66% of civil dockets are land disputes\" is sourceable (NITI
    Aayog/DAKSH

    1.  but currently unsourced. Add the footnote.

## 2.4 P3 --- logic, consistency, structure

1.  The Zoho contradiction: Sec 5.3 argues export-first companies have
    \"no domestic forcing function\" to build floors --- yet Zoho, the
    essay\'s own flagship, is export-first **and** built its own floor.
    Explain Zoho as the exception (founder discipline, no VC pressure,
    the 1996-2002 framework era preceded the SaaS pivot), or soften
    \"the domestic wall is necessary.\"

2.  Section 6.9 (language computing) is a long digression from Section
    6\'s forcing-function through-line. Tighten to one paragraph or move
    to the annexure.

3.  Drove is miscategorized as a low-level \"internal tool.\" It is a
    Floor-layer orchestrator. Recategorize it upward consistently across
    5.2.1, 6.3, and 6.7.

4.  Metadata drift: several :DESCRIPTION: drawers promise content the
    body omits (e.g. 4.1.001 promises \"5.1% growth\" and \"largest
    developer base\"; 3.7.003 promises a transition to Section 4 that
    never lands). Align DESCRIPTIONs with the body, or trim them.

5.  Naming-convention violations: several :CHILDREN: declarations say
    .Tab. while the element heading says .FigCode. Mechanical, but the
    convention only works if it is actually followed.

## 2.5 P4 --- verbosity and conventions

1.  The five patterns are stated twice --- as prose (6.2.3.001) and as a
    table (6.2.3.002). Keep one.

2.  The Drove facts are told three times (5.2.1, 6.4.4.2, 6.7).
    Consolidate --- and see the \"expand Drove\" recommendation below.

3.  The neutral-custody argument appears three times (7.1, 7.3.002,
    7.4). Make 7.3.002 canonical and reduce the others to forward
    references.

4.  The rail/locomotive metaphor is used twice in adjacent elements
    (4.6.003, 4.6.004). Keep one.

5.  Section 4.5 restates 4.2 in the same words; Section 3.4 is a
    two-line stub. Merge/delete.

6.  Five figures are raw HTML/CSS while every other figure uses
    OJS/Mermaid/ Pikchr. Convert them --- they break the document\'s own
    convention and the rendering pipeline.

7.  Section 6.9 presents the same language-ecosystem comparison twice
    (org table

    -   HTML figure). Keep one.

8.  The overall cut target: the essay is \~15% longer than it needs to
    be. The framing and ceremony sentences can go; the examples and
    numbers must stay.

## 2.6 Structural upgrades (things to add, not just fix)

1.  **Give PhonePe Drove a full, detailed story box.** It is the
    essay\'s single best India-built floor-layer artifact and currently
    gets three short mentions. A dedicated story should cover: why Mesos
    failed at PhonePe\'s scale, what Drove actually is (NUMA-aware
    scheduling, leader election, executors, gateway), the decision to
    open-source, and the license/adoption gap. This converts the
    essay\'s strongest \"India hit the wall\" exhibit into a concrete
    case study.

2.  **Reframe the Zoho material.** The essay does not need the company
    history; it needs one point: Zoho began as a near-floor builder
    (lone wolf / garage pattern --- 15 people writing a Java SNMP API
    and WebNMS from scratch) and later kept that floor proprietary. Cut
    the chronology to a sentence.

3.  **Draw the flywheel as a loop.** The \"Commercial Pressure -\>
    Internal Build -\> Open-Source Release -\> Ecosystem Adoption\"
    block is currently a vertical text list. A circular Mermaid loop
    with a return arrow is the whole point; make it self-evident.

4.  **Add a log-scale bar after the TPC-C table.** The \~70× gap between
    #1 and #5 is invisible in rounded table numbers. On a log axis the
    Chinese lead reads instantly and gives the essay its first real
    figure.

# 3. What to keep

Do not touch the following --- they are the reason the essay is worth
the fix list above.

1.  The thesis and the \"renting the floor\" metaphor.
2.  The reframed wall argument (assembly vs. greenfield sovereignty).
3.  The DPI distinction (protocol floor vs. software-engineering floor).
4.  The exceptions autopsy --- \"open-sourced but not governed,\"
    \"re-domiciled to access capital,\" \"moat vs. commons.\" This is
    the best analytical work in the essay.
5.  The falsifiable recommendations (2030 target, land-records project,
    Indian OSS Foundation).

The essay does not need to be re-argued. It needs to be made true. Close
the fact gap and it goes from \"an interesting essay\" to \"an essay
people cite.\"
